title: Here Comes the Sun

alt_voicings.label: Decorations & easier F
alt_voicings.note: hammer sus notes inside D and A; Fmaj7 is the easy stand-in for F

sections.name: Refrain
sections.note: Bar 6 holds three chords (rhythm approximate — follow the record). Last bar is 7/8: count 1-2, 1-2, 1-2-3. Many charts reduce bars 5–8 to D–G–A7.

sections.name: Bridge
sections.note: 11/8 = 3+3+3+2 eighths: one chord per group. Then a 4/4 bar of D and a 7/8 bar of A7.

sections.name: Bridge, last pass
sections.note: The sixth pass: the 7/8 bar becomes four 4/4 bars of A7.

why: Bright open shapes up at the 7th fret with **sus2/sus4 hammer-ons** in a moving strum — and your first **odd meters** (11/8, 7/8), felt as long and short beats.
hard_change: Bridge bar 1: **F → C → G → D inside one 11/8 bar**. Count 1-2-3, 1-2-3, 1-2-3, 1-2 out loud; one chord on each “1”.
theory: Concert key A (capo 7, D shapes): I–IV–V. The bridge is ♭III–♭VII–IV–I (C G D A concert), a Mixolydian cascade; E7 is V/V.
steps: Changes alone, slowly: the bridge chords counted 3+3+3+2, then the 7/8 bar as 2+2+3.
With the rhythm at 70% (about 90 bpm), sus hammer-ons on D and A.
With the record, capo 7. After the refrains the record has an outro; follow it by ear.
